name: IL-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's +5 Democratic lean plus favorable environment
Incumbency and Polymarket pricing near 94% Democratic
No public polling to refine the estimate
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Budzinski: a +5 Democratic district, a favorable national environment, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge, with markets pricing her near certain to win. With no polls available, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based estimate with wide uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late public polling or a surge of Republican outside spending could narrow the margin, though a Wilson win would require a major environment shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term Democrat Nikki Budzinski seeks reelection in an Illinois district that leans Democratic by about five points. She enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised nearly $2.9 million and holding $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Jeff Wilson has raised about $348,000 with only $12,000 available. No outside groups have spent meaningfully against her.

No public general-election polling exists for the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Budzinski around 94 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and resources makes her a strong favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for error.
